primary_source.citation: Toyabe S, Watanabe-Nakayama T, Okamoto T, Kudo S, Muneyuki E. Thermodynamic efficiency and mechanochemical coupling of F1-ATPase. PNAS 108(44):17951-17956 (2011).
primary_source.depth: E1 bibliographic original abstract and indexed original figure/results text; complete methods, supplement and raw figures not independently audited
primary_source.rights: Permission to redistribute publisher text/figures not independently established; original critical paraphrase and URLs only
primary_source.observed: Reversible 120 degree rotations of isolated F1 ATPase with external electrorotation torque and imposed ATP/ADP/phosphate chemical potentials
primary_source.scope_caution: Near chemical-free-energy work per stalled transition does not establish positive sustained load power or complete manufacturing and lifetime net output; low-nucleotide conditions can depart from tight coupling

ora_interpretation: Ora COHERENT-CONTACT-01 retired through PR113 for no complete source/load/all-role renewal; isolated association kernel exported zero useful work, not a full-candidate negative experiment.
decision: Retain isolated motor as a measurable work-vs-torque reference only; do not reinstate retired Ora mechanism, assume no-cost repair, or infer a self-renewing constructor from motor efficiency.

future_only_hypotheses.hypothesis: A molecular motor with high component-level efficiency may deliver nonpositive lifetime net surplus after fully paid formation, renewal and retained-load hardware costs.
future_only_hypotheses.refutation: A complete independently audited raw-start failure-inclusive lifetime ledger shows positive surplus over an attainable simpler same-feed converter.

future_only_hypotheses.hypothesis: High step work at stall cannot itself produce positive steady mean rotational power at zero average angular velocity.
future_only_hypotheses.refutation: A physically consistent, externally measured rate-dependent power curve demonstrating positive mean rotational power at precisely zero mean angular velocity under steady stall conditions.
